tagline: A 22-nm commuter spine to a no-car island — the textbook foiling-electric replacement
summary: Catalina Express carries roughly 1.3M passengers a year on a fleet of 8 diesel catamarans, with up to 30 daily departures from Long Beach, San Pedro and Dana Point to Avalon (~22 nm) and Two Harbors. The crossing is high-frequency, congestion-prone and weather-exposed on aging hulls — squarely inside the Pioneer II's range and exactly the profile a foiling-electric vessel improves on for comfort, wake and emissions. Avalon's no-car island layers a premium hospitality tier on top of a genuine commuter spine.
competitive_landscape: Catalina Express is the dominant incumbent (a fleet of 8, ~1.3M pax/yr, up to 30 departures/day); the Catalina Flyer runs seasonally from Newport Beach. All are diesel catamarans. There is no foiling or zero-emission operator on the channel today — the comfort gap (a rough, weather-exposed crossing) and the wake/emissions profile in Avalon's small harbor are the open lanes.

demand_signals.value: Long Beach ↔ Avalon ≈ 22 nm, ~1 hr — well inside Pioneer II's 70-nm range

demand_signals.label: No-car island
demand_signals.value: Avalon strictly limits cars (multi-year waitlists; golf carts dominate) — a clean arrival experience matches the island's character

regulatory_note: California's CARB Commercial Harbor Craft regulation is pushing operators toward zero-emission and tier-4+ powertrains, and the Cabrillo Mole ferry terminal in Avalon is under an intermodal revitalization project — both are timing levers for a clean-vessel entry with shore-power/charging integration.
seasonality: Year-round commuter + freight base load with a strong summer leisure peak (Jun–Sep) and event spikes (Catalina events, JazzTrax, races). Weather-exposed crossing means winter comfort is a real differentiator.

navier_fit: High. A short, high-frequency, weather-exposed, congestion-prone diesel crossing into a no-car luxury island is the cleanest possible match for a foiling-electric Pioneer II: comfort and emissions are the precise pain points, the distance sits mid-range, and CARB + the Cabrillo Mole revitalization create the regulatory and infrastructure timing.
